summary: An S&P Global Commodity Insights news article dated 20 Feb 2024 reports that French gas consumption fell further in the week to Feb. 18, 2024, to 9.2 TWh, despite a rebound in power-sector gas demand, based on weekly data published by grid operator GRTgaz. The article also covers the cumulative August 2023 to February 2024 decline versus the 2018-19 reference winter, broken down by sector, and notes that French prompt gas prices remain among Europe's cheapest. The rest of the page is site navigation and subscription boilerplate.
one_line: French gas consumption fell to 9.2 TWh in the week to Feb. 18, 2024 despite a power-sector demand rebound, per GRTgaz data.
key_facts: French gas consumption totaled 9.2 TWh in the week to Feb. 18, 2024, a seven-week low, down from 9.4 TWh the week prior.
The 9.2 TWh weekly consumption was the lowest level since the last week of 2023.
Consumption for public distribution dropped week on week by 9% to 6.4 TWh as temperatures remained relatively high for the time of year.
Consumption by industry connected to the gas grid was flat at 2.4 TWh in the week to Feb. 18, 2024.
Power sector gas demand was 0.4 TWh in the week to Feb. 18, up from 0.1 TWh in the week to Feb. 11.
GRTgaz resumed publication of weekly gas consumption data for the winter at the end of October to reflect French efforts to save gas.
Platts assessed the PEG day-ahead price at Eur22.63/MWh on Feb. 19, a discount of Eur0.70/MWh to the TTF equivalent assessment.
French gas consumption totaled 227.7 TWh over Aug. 1, 2023-Feb. 18, 2024, down 25% versus the same period in 2018-19.
GRTgaz used 2018-19 as the reference winter because it was the last winter before the pandemic, with temperatures within the seasonal average and no particular cold spells.
Corrected for weather, the reduction in gas consumption over Aug. 1, 2023-Feb. 18, 2024 was 20.1%.
Consumption for public distribution was down 22.3% at 147.3 TWh over Aug. 1, 2023-Feb. 18, 2024, due to more favorable weather and gas savings by consumers.
Weather-corrected public distribution consumption fell 14.6% over Aug. 1, 2023-Feb. 18, 2024.
Industry connected to the gas grid consumed 64.1 TWh over Aug. 1, 2023-Feb. 18, 2024, a fall of 24.8%.
Power-sector gas consumption was 43.3% lower at 16.3 TWh over Aug. 1, 2023-Feb. 18, 2024, due to greater nuclear availability, significant renewable generation and power savings efforts.
